s1.syndrome_frame: Worsening skin condition with systemic symptoms in a patient with a history of autoimmune disorders
salient_findings: Diffuse ill-defined erythema and mild edema of the face and eyelids
Violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints, periungual skin, and chest
Fatigue and difficulty with physical activities
key_facts: Patient has a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis
Patient has a history of juvenile dermatomyositis (DM)
Juvenile DM had been in remission for several years
Previous treatments included adalimumab, etanercept, methotrexate, guselkumab, ustekinumab, and topical corticosteroids
DM had remained stable during treatment with anti-TNF and anti-IL-12/23 medications
Patient experienced fatigue, difficulty picking up her child, and climbing stairs after starting new medication
Physical examination revealed diffuse ill-defined erythema and mild edema of the face and eyelids
Laboratory evaluation results were negative or normal, including creatine kinase and aldolase levels

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of biopsy-proven juvenile dermatomyositis and is experiencing worsening skin condition with systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis and is experiencing worsening skin condition

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is experiencing systemic symptoms and has a history of autoimmune disorders, making lupus a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Polymyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is experiencing muscle weakness and has a history of autoimmune myopathy, making polymyositis a possible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of multiple autoimmune disorders and is experiencing overlapping symptoms, making mixed connective tissue disease a possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's history of biopsy-proven juvenile dermatomyositis, along with the presence of characteristic skin findings such as violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints and photodistributed poikiloderma, supports this diagnosis. Additionally, the patient's symptoms of fatigue and muscle weakness, as evidenced by difficulty picking up her child and climbing stairs, are consistent with a flare of dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Psoriasis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of psoriasis, the current presentation with muscle weakness and characteristic dermatomyositis skin findings suggests a flare of dermatomyositis rather than a psoriasis flare.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: There is no mention of other systemic symptoms or laboratory findings typical of lupus, such as joint pain, kidney involvement, or positive autoantibodies.

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: The presence of characteristic skin findings, such as violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints, is more consistent with dermatomyositis than polymyositis, which typically presents with muscle weakness alone.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: There is no mention of other autoimmune diseases or antibodies, such as anti-U1-RNP, that are typically seen in mixed connective tissue disease.
